title: Navigation menus and meaningful link text
learningObjectives: Build meaningful and safe hyperlinks and navigation

understand.concept: Use nav to group major navigation links. Each link needs a clear accessible name; do not use a button for navigation or an anchor for an action that changes application state.
understand.whyItMatters: Correct semantics make site navigation predictable for all users and assistive technologies.
understand.analogy: A link is like a reference in an index that takes a reader to another place.
understand.analogyLimit: A web link can navigate across pages, domains, protocols or app actions; it is not exactly a printed index.

explain.narrative: Use nav to group major navigation links. Each link needs a clear accessible name; do not use a button for navigation or an anchor for an action that changes application state.

examples.explanation: href specifies the destination. Write link text that makes sense out of context; consider privacy and security when navigating externally.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser displays a meaningful link that navigates to its destination when activated.

practise.guidedTask: Modify the H4.6 example and add your own destination.
practise.independentTask: Create a navigation bar with Home, Courses, About and Contact links and verify every destination.
hints: Use anchors for navigation and buttons for page actions.
